context:
Add execute.platform_chunking so a sweep runs one platform at a time and prunes
databases between chunks through the existing reuse-aware cleanup helpers.
Extend preflight_budget to model per-platform database footprint times platform
count and either auto-enable chunking or fail preflight with the specific
shortfall, instead of exhausting disk mid-sweep.
description:
Release-gate stage 1 exhausted disk twice on 2026-08-04 (at 2.7 GB and 4 GB free)
and had to be killed mid-sweep, which then hit the orphan defect tracked in
uat-cell-teardown-orphans-child-processes.

The cause is structural, not incidental: loaded databases are per-platform and
measured roughly 15 GB each, so 11 platforms need 90-150 GB concurrently. The
existing preflight budget does not model that, so the sweep passes preflight and
then dies partway through.

The workaround that did complete stage 1 was an out-of-tree shell driver running
one platform at a time and pruning databases between chunks. That mechanism
belongs in the framework rather than in a scratch script.

anti_patterns.dont: hardcode 15 GB as the per-platform footprint
anti_patterns.instead: derive from the configured scale rungs and record the basis in the lifecycle log
anti_patterns.why: it is one measurement at one scale ladder and will silently mislead at other scales

anti_patterns.dont: leave chunking as an out-of-tree shell script
anti_patterns.instead: land it as a config-driven execute mode with tests
anti_patterns.why: the scratch driver from 2026-08-04 was lost when the scratchpad was wiped, taking the only working stage-1 recipe with it

anti_patterns.dont: let preflight pass and discover the shortfall mid-sweep
anti_patterns.instead: fail preflight with the computed shortfall, or auto-enable chunking
anti_patterns.why: that is the current behavior and it costs hours plus an orphaned process cleanup every time

anti_patterns.dont: prune the whole databases root between chunks
anti_patterns.instead: prune per (platform, benchmark, scale) through the existing helpers
anti_patterns.why: it destroys the intentional cross-benchmark reuse cleanup.py exists to protect and silently inflates load times

preserves.behavior: A single cells.jsonl stream and its .inprogress/.finalized markers remain the authoritative per-sweep record across chunks.
Release-gate stage ordering (native, then docker non-OLTP, then docker OLTP) is unchanged; chunking operates within a stage.
Reuse-aware pruning boundaries in cleanup.py are unchanged -- chunk pruning calls them, it does not bypass them.
preserve_datagen: true and datagen reuse across chunks are unchanged; only loaded databases are pruned.

prior_art.concept: reuse-aware pruning already knows the safe reuse boundaries (TPC-H databases reused by read_primitives); chunk pruning must go through it, not rm -rf
platform group enumeration already drives the sweep order; chunking iterates the same enumeration rather than defining its own
existing budget estimator and headroom gate; extend with the per-platform database term rather than adding a second estimator

verifications.description: Preflight budget tests cover the per-platform database term and the shortfall message
verifications.expected: budget accounts for platform count; insufficient disk fails preflight with the computed shortfall

verifications.command: uv run -- python -m pytest tests/uat/test_cleanup.py tests/uat/test_phases.py -q -k chunk
verifications.description: Chunked execution prunes between chunks through the reuse-aware helpers
verifications.expected: at least one test collected and passing

verifications.command: uv run python -c "from tests.uat.config import ExecuteConfig as E;assert 'platform_chunking' in E.__dataclass_fields__"
verifications.description: platform_chunking is a real execute config field

work_units.summary: Model per-platform database footprint in the preflight budget
Fail preflight with the computed shortfall instead of exhausting disk mid-sweep
Add execute platform_chunking running one platform at a time
Prune between chunks via the reuse-aware cleanup helpers
Document the chunked mode and its disk math in the operator guide
